confidentUnsupported.evidence: the issue lies with the start control system. This requires assessment by an appliance engineer.

rationale: The assistant acknowledged the 4C code but never interpreted it as a water-supply error, instead running a generic 'won't start' script (door, child lock, delay start) that ignored the error code entirely. Even after the customer volunteered that there is no water in the tub and a plumber worked under the sink yesterday, it ignored this decisive evidence and confidently declared a 'start control system' fault needing an engineer. The real cause was an isolation valve left closed, a trivial check the assistant never asked; the homeowner would be sent to pay for an unnecessary engineer visit.
